meanings: I don't know where to start (from being tired or busy)
I don't know which way to turn
forms: literally: I don't know where I'm hitting

examples.sr: Толико посла имам да [не зна̑м где̏ у̏дарам].
examples.en: I have so much work that I don't know where to start.

forms: literally: I can eat an ox

examples.sr: Од јутрос ништа нисам јео, [мо̀гу во̀ла да по̀једе̄м].
examples.en: I haven't eaten anything since this morning, I could eat a horse.

meanings: to roll on the floor laughing
to be doubled over with laughter

examples.en: We were all rolling with laughter.

meanings: my legs are about to fall off (tired after a long walk)

examples.en: After the walk my legs are about to fall off.

examples.sr: Кад сам чуо тај звук, [ср̏це ми је ста̏ло].
examples.en: When I heard that sound, my heart stopped.

examples.sr: Када је ауто закочио, [у̏мро сам од стра̑ха].
examples.en: When the car braked hard, I almost died of fear.

key: phr:смем ли да помазим вашег пса

examples.en: May I pet your dog?

note: Polite way to ask the owner; the usual answer is «Може!»

key: phr:упала му је секира у мед
meanings: he struck it lucky, an easy success
forms: literally: his axe fell into honey

examples.sr: [У̏пала му је сѐкира у ме̑д], нашао је стан за мало новца.
examples.en: He got a lucky break: he found an apartment for little money.
Luck smiled on him at the exam.

meanings: God looked after him, he was lucky

examples.sr: [Бо̑г га је поглѐдао], избегао је несрећу.
examples.en: God looked after him, he avoided the accident.

meanings: things started going well for him

examples.sr: После много труда најзад [му је кре́нуло] на послу.
examples.en: After a lot of effort, things finally started going well for him at work.

examples.sr: [Посрѐћило му се] да нађе паркинг у центру.
examples.en: He got lucky and found a parking spot downtown.

forms: literally: everything fell into the water

examples.sr: Због кише [све̏ је па̏ло у во̏ду].
examples.en: Because of the rain, everything fell through.

meanings: all my ships have sunk, everything is lost

examples.sr: Кад је изгубио посао, [све̏ ла̏ђе су му пото̀нуле].
examples.en: When he lost his job, everything was lost.

examples.sr: Од јутра [је све̏ кре́нуло по злу̏].
examples.en: Everything has gone wrong since this morning.

examples.sr: Откад је остао без посла, [све̏ му је кре́нуло ни̏збрдо].
examples.en: Ever since he lost his job, everything has gone downhill for him.

key: phr:ништа ми не полази за руком

examples.sr: Данас [ни̏шта ми не по̀лази за ру́ко̄м].
examples.en: Nothing is working out for me today.

key: phr:ништа ми не иде од руке
meanings: everything is going wrong for me

examples.sr: Данас [ни̏шта ми не и̏де од ру̏ке].
examples.en: Everything is going wrong for me today.

meanings: to get up on the wrong side of the bed

examples.sr: Изгледа да је данас [у̀стао на ле̏ву но̏гу].
examples.en: Looks like he got up on the wrong side of the bed today.
I completely flunked the exam.

note: Colloquial, for a complete failure.

examples.sr: Једна грешка и [све̏ о̏де у три̏ лѐпе].
examples.en: One mistake and everything goes down the drain.

note: A mild replacement for a vulgar expression.

examples.sr: Нама се све срушило [ка̏о ку́ла од ка̏ра̄та̄].
examples.en: Everything collapsed for us like a house of cards.
I've been trying for a long time, but I can't get it right.

meanings: it wasn't meant to be for me

examples.sr: Покушао сам, али [нѝје ми би̏ло су̏ђено].
examples.en: I tried, but it wasn't meant to be.

meanings: as if bad luck is following me

examples.sr: Шта год урадим, [ка̏о да ме пра̏ти ма̏лер].
examples.en: Whatever I do, it's as if bad luck is following me.

meanings: whoever cursed me didn't waste their time (jokingly, about a streak of bad luck)

examples.sr: Опет ми је све пошло наопако: [ко̏ ме кле̏о, нѝје да̀нгубио].
examples.en: Everything has gone wrong for me again: whoever cursed me didn't waste their time.

note: Jokey; «дангубити» means to waste time.

examples.sr: Данас [су̑нце пр̏жи] тако да је немогуће бити напољу без капе.
examples.en: The sun is so scorching today that you can't be outside without a hat.

note: Also «сунце пече»; for strong summer sun.

examples.sr: Данас сам [у фа̏зону] да не радим ништа.
examples.en: Today I'm in the mood to do nothing.

note: Colloquial.

examples.en: Take it easy, there's time, don't get nervous.

note: The main mantra of everyday life, from the bank to work meetings.

forms: literally: we lived and we saw

examples.sr: Шта ће бити? [Жи̏ви би̏ли па ви̏дели]!
examples.en: What will happen? We'll see!

meanings: be quiet, it could be worse

examples.sr: Изгубили смо новац, али [ћу̏ти, мо̏же и го̏ре].
examples.en: We lost money, but hush, it could be worse.

note: Serbian consolation: be glad it isn't worse.

examples.en: Football is not my cup of tea.

note: A calque from English.

key: phr:шта је писац хтео да каже
meanings: what did the author mean to say? (ironic, about unclear speech)

examples.sr: Остало ми није јасно: [шта̏ је пи́сац хте̏о да ка̏же]?
examples.en: The rest wasn't clear to me: what was the author trying to say?

note: A school question, repeated ironically when someone speaks unclearly.

examples.sr: Знао је истину, али је [др̏жао јѐзик за зу́бима].
examples.en: He knew the truth, but he held his tongue.

meanings: to get the short end of the stick

examples.en: He got the short end of the stick in the argument.

meanings: to have someone in one's grip
to have someone under one's thumb

examples.sr: Зна његове тајне и [др̀жи га у ша̏ци].
examples.en: He knows his secrets and has him under his thumb.

meanings: to bang one's head against a wall
to be stubborn and push ahead regardless

examples.sr: Не слуша савете, увек [и̏де гла́во̄м кроз зи̑д].
examples.en: He doesn't listen to advice, he always charges ahead regardless.

examples.sr: [Прѐврнуо је не̏бо и зе̏мљу] да нађе решење.
examples.en: He moved heaven and earth to find a solution.

examples.sr: После грешке на послу [о̑н је на та̏нком ле̏ду].
examples.en: After the mistake at work, he's on thin ice.

examples.sr: У расправи је најбоље било [спу̀стити ло̏пту].
examples.en: In the argument, the best thing was to tone it down.

meanings: to turn a blind eye to something

examples.sr: Не треба [затва́рати о̏чи] пред очигледним проблемима.
examples.en: We shouldn't turn a blind eye to obvious problems.

forms: literally: I'm treating a round

examples.en: Today I'm buying everyone a round.
Who's buying this round?
Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
How do I get to the city center?

note: Be polite: «Извините, молим вас...»

forms: literally: you can't miss

examples.sr: Хотел је на углу, [не мо̏жеш да про̏машиш].
examples.en: The hotel is on the corner, you can't miss it.

examples.sr: Видећеш велики натпис, [не мо̏жеш да про̏машиш].
examples.en: You'll see a big sign, you can't miss it.

examples.sr: Не брини, [јо̏ш ма̏ло па си ту̑].
examples.en: Don't worry, you're almost there.
Cross the street at the crosswalk.
There's a new crosswalk near the school.

note: Colloquially «зебра».

examples.sr: - Знаш ли ти њега? - [Чу̑ј зна̑м]! То ми је брат!
examples.en: - Do you know him? - Of course I do! He's my brother!

note: «чуј» before a verb makes an indignant «and how!» or «of course».

examples.en: We will continue regardless of the obstacles.
I'll come regardless of being tired.

examples.sr: [С о̏бзиром на] гужву, кренули смо раније.
examples.en: Given the traffic jam, we left earlier.

examples.sr: [С о̏бзиром на] време, остајемо код куће.
examples.en: Given the weather, we're staying home.
The candidate's experience should be taken into account.

examples.sr: Молим вас да [у̏зме̄те у о̏бзӣр] моје стање.
examples.en: Please take my condition into account.

forms: literally: it doesn't come into consideration

examples.en: Being late is out of the question.
Selling the house is out of the question.

note: The opposite is «долази у обзир»: it is suitable, possible.

examples.en: Be considerate toward the sick.
You should be considerate of your neighbors.

meanings: let it sit there, it doesn't cost anything (about a spare)
forms: literally: let it stand, it doesn't eat bread

examples.sr: Узми и то, [не̏ка сто̀јӣ, хле̏ба не је̏де].
examples.en: Take that too, it doesn't hurt to have it.

examples.sr: Купио сам још једну, [не̏ка сто̀јӣ, хле̏ба не је̏де].
examples.en: I bought another one, let it sit there, it doesn't cost anything to keep.

note: Said about something bought in reserve that bothers no one.

forms: literally: he has no hair on his tongue

examples.sr: Он је искрен, [не̑ма дла̏ке на јѐзику].
examples.en: He's honest, he doesn't mince words.
My aunt says everything straight to your face.

meanings: he splits hairs, he looks for a flaw
forms: literally: he looks for a hair in an egg

examples.en: The boss is always nitpicking.

examples.sr: Не [тра̏жи дла̏ку у ја̏јету], све је у реду.
examples.en: Don't nitpick, everything is fine.

forms: literally: by a hair

examples.sr: Аутобус је прошао [за дла̏ку] поред нас.
examples.en: The bus missed us by a hair.
We avoided the accident by a hair.

key: phr:вук длаку мења, али ћуд никад
meanings: a leopard can't change its spots
forms: literally: the wolf changes its coat, but never its temper

examples.sr: Многи кажу: [ву̑к дла̏ку ме̏ња, а̏ли ћу̑д ни̏кад].
examples.en: Many say: a wolf changes its coat, but never its nature.

note: «ћуд» means temper, character.

forms: literally: goes along with the fur

examples.sr: Колеге му [и̏ду ни̑з дла̏ку] да нема свађе.
examples.en: His colleagues humor him so there are no quarrels.

examples.sr: Не мораш да му [и̏деш ни̑з дла̏ку].
examples.en: You don't have to go along with everything he says.
Excuse me, what time is it?
What time is it now?

note: Colloquially also «Колико има сати?»

forms: literally: half (to) three

examples.en: See you at half past two.
Lunch is at half past twelve.

note: «пола» + the next hour: «пола пет» = 4:30

examples.en: We'll arrive at five to three.
The train leaves at ten to four.

note: Minutes «до» + the next hour: «петнаест до шест» = 5:45

examples.en: I don't want to wait.
She doesn't want to talk to me.

note: «нећу» + да + present tense: refusal, unwillingness; «нећу доћи» is a plain future: I won't come

meanings: long hair, short on brains (about a shallow person)
forms: literally: long hair, short mind

examples.sr: Не слушај је, [ду́га ко̀са, кра̏тка па̏ме̄т].
examples.en: Don't listen to her, long hair, short on brains.

note: A mocking and rather rude proverb; better not to say it to a woman.

forms: literally: where was your mind

examples.sr: Заборавио си кључеве у ауту? [Где̏ ти је па̏ме̄т би́ла]?
examples.en: You left the keys in the car? Where was your head?

examples.sr: [Где̏ ти је па̏ме̄т би́ла] кад си то рекао?
examples.en: What were you thinking when you said that?

meanings: he's luckier than he is smart
forms: literally: he has more luck than sense

examples.en: He's luckier than he is smart.

examples.sr: Прошао је без повреда, [и̏ма ви̏ше сре̏ће не̏го па̏мети].
examples.en: He got away without injuries, he has more luck than sense.

note: About someone who did something stupid and still got away with it.

key: phr:као да је попио сву памет света
forms: literally: as if he drank all the wisdom of the world

examples.sr: Прича [ка̏о да је по̀пио сву̏ па̏ме̄т све̑та].
examples.en: He talks as if he had all the wisdom in the world.

examples.sr: Ћути, нећеш ти [по̀пити сву̏ па̏ме̄т све̑та].
examples.en: Be quiet, you're not smarter than everyone else.

meanings: don't tell me what to do
forms: literally: don't salt my mind

examples.sr: [Не̏мој да ми со̏лиш па̏ме̄т], знам шта радим.
examples.en: Don't lecture me, I know what I'm doing.
My colleague is constantly lecturing me.

note: About unsolicited advice.

meanings: can you take a picture of me?

examples.sr: [Мо̏жеш ли да ме сли̏каш] испред зграде?
examples.en: Can you take a picture of me in front of the building?
Excuse me, could you take a picture of us?
Well done, you got a good shot.
Can I pay by card?
You can pay by card here.

meanings: to tap the card (on the terminal)

examples.en: Tap your card on the terminal.
Just tap your card and you're done.
My card was declined at the terminal.

meanings: to pick a fight with someone
to get into it with someone

examples.sr: Не [зака̀чи се с њи̑м], опасан је.
examples.en: Don't mess with him, he's dangerous.
He's picked a fight with someone again.

examples.sr: [Све̏ у свѐму], била је то добра одлука.
examples.en: All in all, it was a good decision.
All in all, we had a good rest.

meanings: I would like to make an appointment (with a doctor)

examples.sr: Добар дан, [жѐлела бих да за̀кажем пре́глед].
examples.en: Good afternoon, I would like to make an appointment.

examples.sr: [Жѐлео бих да за̀кажем пре́глед] за четвртак.
examples.en: I would like to make an appointment for Thursday.

note: A man says «желео бих».

examples.sr: Докторе, [не о̀сећам се до̀бро] већ три дана.
examples.en: Doctor, I haven't been feeling well for three days.
Excuse me, I don't feel well.
I'm allergic to penicillin.
She's allergic to pollen.

meanings: I find it hard to breathe

examples.sr: Од јутрос [те̑шко ми је да ди̏шем].
examples.en: I've had trouble breathing since this morning.
I find it hard to sleep.
Call an ambulance, please!
Quick, call an ambulance!
Next week I'm defending my thesis.

examples.sr: Студент је [бра̏нио ма̏стер ра̑д] пред комисијом.
examples.en: The student defended his master's thesis before the committee.

note: The defense itself is «одбрана».

examples.en: Get out of here! I didn't tell you anything.
Scram, man!

note: Very rude, from Turkish; «сиктер бре» means get lost.

meanings: I didn't get a wink of sleep
forms: literally: I haven't closed an eye

examples.en: I didn't sleep a wink all night.
Because of the heat, we didn't sleep a wink.

forms: literally: it pokes the eyes

examples.sr: Та слика криво виси и [бо̀де о̏чи].
examples.en: That picture hangs crooked and it's an eyesore.

key: phr:не могу га очима да видим
meanings: I can't stand the sight of him

examples.sr: Од тог комшије [не мо̀гу га о̏чима да ви̏дӣм].
examples.en: I can't stand the sight of that neighbor.
I can't stand the sight of her.

note: About a woman: «не могу је очима да видим»

key: phr:далеко од очију, далеко од срца
meanings: out of sight, out of mind

examples.sr: [Далѐко од о̀чијӯ, далѐко од ср̏ца], каже пословица.
examples.en: Out of sight, out of mind, as the saying goes.

forms: literally: I'm boiling

examples.en: I'm boiling in this bus.
Everyone is boiling at thirty degrees.
I'm melting from the heat.
What are you doing? I'm melting in the sun.

meanings: I've turned into a crackling (very sunburnt or overheated)

examples.sr: После сата на плажи [претво̀рио сам се у чва́рак].
examples.en: After an hour on the beach, I've turned into a crackling.

key: phr:није што је вруће, него што је спарина
meanings: it's not the heat, it's the humidity

examples.sr: [Нѝје што̏ је вру̏ће, не̏го што̏ је спа̀рина], не могу да дишем.
examples.en: It's not the heat, it's the humidity, I can't breathe.

note: A summer saying-meme about muggy weather.

examples.sr: Ако изађем у подне, [до̏бӣћу то̏плотни у̏да̄р].
examples.en: If I go out at noon, I'm going to get heatstroke.

examples.sr: У овој соби [не мо̏же да се ди̏ше].
examples.en: You can't breathe in this room.

examples.sr: Напољу [не мо̏же да се ди̏ше] од врућине.
examples.en: You can't breathe outside in this heat.
Give me some water, I'm dying of heat.

note: «цркох» is a jokey aorist of «цркнути»; rather rude, colloquial.

examples.en: - See you at six? - Okay!
- Can I sit here? - Sure.

note: The most common affirmative reply in conversation.

examples.en: - Do you want to come with us? - Why not?
Coffee? Why not!

examples.sr: - Можеш ли да ми помогнеш? - [Не̑ма про̀блема].
examples.en: - Can you help me? - No problem.
No problem, I'll be there on time.
- See you tomorrow at ten. - It's a deal.

forms: literally: to raise dust

examples.sr: Његов коментар је [ди̏гао пра̀шину] на мрежама.
examples.en: His comment caused a stir on social media.
That article will cause a stir.
If you read between the lines, you'll understand the truth.
I know how to read between the lines.

meanings: the pen is mightier than the sword

examples.sr: Договорили су се мирно, [ре̑ч је ја̀ча̄ од ма̏ча].
examples.en: They settled it peacefully, words are stronger than swords.

forms: literally: to the crate

examples.en: Come over to my place!

note: In slang «гајба» means a flat or home; literally a crate (for beer).

key: phr:као да му је из ока испао
meanings: the spitting image of (his father, mother)
forms: literally: as if he fell out of his eye

examples.sr: Син је оцу [ка̏о да му је из о̏ка ѝспао].
examples.en: The son is the spitting image of his father.

examples.sr: Ћерка је мајци [ка̏о да јој је из о̏ка испа̀ла].
examples.en: The daughter is the spitting image of her mother.

meanings: to not take one's eyes off someone
to not take one's eyes off

examples.sr: Целе вечери [нѝје ски̏дао о̏чи с ње̑].
examples.en: He didn't take his eyes off her all evening.
The mother doesn't take her eyes off the child.

examples.sr: Разговор са њом ми је [отво̀рио о̏чи].
examples.en: Talking to her opened my eyes.
I want to open your eyes.

key: phr:на једно уво уђе, на друго изађе
meanings: it goes in one ear and out the other

examples.sr: Шта год му кажеш, [на је̏дно у̏во у̏ђе, на дру̏го и̏зађе].
examples.en: Whatever you tell him, it goes in one ear and out the other.

forms: literally: to break one's head

examples.sr: Већ два дана [ра̏збијам гла̑ву] над овим проблемом.
examples.en: I've been racking my brain over this problem for two days.
Don't rack your brain, it'll be fine.

meanings: I can't wrap my head around it
it makes no sense to me
forms: literally: it doesn't go into my head

examples.sr: [Не и̏де ми у гла̑ву] зашто је то урадио.
examples.en: I can't wrap my head around why he did that.

meanings: to have one's head in the clouds

examples.sr: На часу је стално [с гла́во̄м у о̏бла̄цима].
examples.en: He always has his head in the clouds in class.
He always has his head in the clouds.

key: phr:не кајем се због своје тетоваже

examples.sr: Прошло је десет година и [не ка̏јем се збо̏г сво̀је тето̀важе].
examples.en: Ten years have passed and I don't regret my tattoo.
Everyone passed the exam.
I hope I'll pass the exam.

note: «пасти на испиту» means to fail an exam.

examples.en: I would like to go to the cinema.
I would like to try this dish.

note: A man says «волео бих», a woman «волела бих»; softer than «хоћу» and «желим».

meanings: that's the first I've heard of it
I'm hearing about it for the first time

examples.en: That's the first I've heard of it!

examples.sr: Извини, [пр̀ви пу̑т чу̏је̄м за то̑] место.
examples.en: Sorry, I've never heard of that place.

examples.sr: Не питај ме, [ни́сам упу̀ћен у то̑].
examples.en: Don't ask me, I'm not in the loop.
She hasn't been told the details.

forms: literally: that's a Spanish village to me

examples.en: Math is all Greek to me.

examples.sr: То ми је [шпа̏нско сѐло], не разумем ништа.
examples.en: It's all Greek to me, I don't understand anything.
Where did he go? God only knows.
God only knows when he'll come.
Come in, make yourself at home.

examples.sr: Молим вас, [осѐћајте се ка̏о ко̏д ку̏ће].
examples.en: Please, make yourself at home.

examples.sr: - Не знам како ћу све стићи! - [Ма̏ ла̏гано]!
examples.en: - I don't know how I'll get everything done! - Come on, take it easy!
Take it easy, there's time.

examples.sr: - Морамо одмах да кренемо. - Полако, [и̏ма вре̏мена].
examples.en: - We have to leave right now. - Easy, there's time.
Don't rush, there's time.

examples.sr: - Шеф је љут на мене! - [Не ло̏жи се].
examples.en: - The boss is angry at me! - Don't get worked up.

note: Colloquial.

forms: literally: it will be

examples.sr: - Бојим се да нећу моћи да купим. - Ма [би́ће].
examples.en: - I'm afraid I won't be able to buy it. - Come on, it'll work out.

note: Reassuring, without forcing events.

forms: literally: you bang like Maxim at a division

examples.sr: Не слушај га, [лу̏па ка̏о Ма̏ксим по дивѝзији].
examples.en: Don't listen to him, he's talking nonsense.

note: Максим is either a gunner or the «Maxim» machine gun.

forms: literally: drunk like a mother

examples.sr: Синоћ је дошао кући [пѝјан ка̏о ма̑јка].
examples.en: Last night he came home dead drunk.

note: By one version, women in labor were given rakija as a painkiller.

key: phr:као да је пао с крушке
meanings: as if he just dropped from the sky, clueless
as if he were born yesterday
forms: literally: as if he fell from a pear tree

examples.sr: Шта ме гледаш [ка̏о да си па̏о с кру̏шке]?
examples.en: Why are you looking at me like you just dropped from the sky?

forms: literally: to thresh empty straw

examples.sr: Не [мла̏ти пра̏зну сла̏му], реци шта хоћеш.
examples.en: Don't talk nonsense, say what you want.

meanings: to pull the wool over someone's eyes
forms: literally: to sell fog

examples.sr: Он само [про̀даје ма̏глу] и ништа не ради.
examples.en: He only feeds people a line and does nothing.
Don't feed people a line.
Sorry, my connection is breaking up.
My connection is breaking up, we'll talk later.

examples.sr: [Сла̏бо те чу̏је̄м], можеш ли да поновиш?
examples.en: I can barely hear you, can you repeat that?
Sorry, I can barely hear you.

meanings: the video froze on my end

examples.en: Wait, my picture froze.
The internet went down in the whole building.

examples.sr: [Да ли ме са̏да чу̏је̄ш] и видиш?
examples.en: Can you hear and see me now?

examples.sr: Мало сам променио везу, [да ли ме са̏да чу̏је̄те]?
examples.en: I changed my connection a bit, can you hear me now?

meanings: to cost an arm and a leg
forms: literally: to cost like Saint Petka's scrambled eggs

examples.sr: Овај стан [ко̏шта ка̏о све̏те Пе̏тке ка̏јгана].
examples.en: This apartment costs a fortune.

note: Its origin is linked to religious traditions.

meanings: to come to a bad end
forms: literally: to pick a green melon patch

examples.en: If you do that, you'll be in big trouble.

meanings: the day of reckoning has come
the devil has come to collect
forms: literally: the devil has come for his own

examples.sr: Годинама је варао људе, сада је [до̏шао ђа̏во̄ по сво̀је].
examples.en: For years he deceived people, now the day of reckoning has come.

meanings: like a chicken with its head cut off
forms: literally: like a chick in tow fibers

examples.sr: Без плана сам [ка̏о пи̏ле у ку̏чине].
examples.en: Without a plan I'm completely lost.

examples.sr: Била је [ка̏о пи̏ле у ку̏чине] међу папирима.
examples.en: She was completely lost among the papers.

meanings: to go from bad to worse
to come down in the world
forms: literally: fell from a horse onto a donkey

examples.sr: Променио је посао и [па̏о с ко̀ња на ма̀гарца].
examples.en: He changed jobs and things got worse.

forms: literally: to go with one's throat into the strawberries

examples.en: Don't rush headlong, think it over.
He always rushes in headlong.

meanings: to be at war with each other
forms: literally: to be on a war footing

examples.sr: Комшије су [на ра̏тној но̀зи] због музике.
examples.en: The neighbors are at daggers drawn over the music.

examples.sr: Брат и ја смо [на ра̏тној но̀зи].
examples.en: My brother and I aren't speaking.

meanings: to not be able to stand each other
forms: literally: to not smell each other

examples.en: The Petrovićes don't get along with their neighbors.

meanings: to not be on good terms
forms: literally: to not be in love

examples.sr: Они [ни́су у љу́бави] од прошле године.
examples.en: They've been on cool terms since last year.

note: Ironic.

forms: literally: to not close

examples.en: Granny Mara talks and talks and never shuts her mouth!

note: Colloquial.

key: phr:први мачићи се у воду бацају
meanings: the first attempt is always the roughest
forms: literally: the first kittens are thrown into the water

examples.sr: Не жали, [пр̀ви ма̀чићи се у во̏ду ба̏цају].
examples.en: Don't feel bad, the first attempt is always the roughest.

meanings: to be out of one's mind
forms: literally: to eat henbane

examples.en: What's wrong with you, have you lost your mind?

meanings: to be on pins and needles
to sit on pins and needles

examples.sr: Чекао је резултате и [се̏део ка̏о на ѝглама].
examples.en: He was waiting for the results and sitting on pins and needles.

key: phr:као да је пао с марса
meanings: as if he just dropped from Mars
as if he's from another planet

examples.sr: Гледа ме [ка̏о да је па̏о с Ма̑рса].
examples.en: He's looking at me as if he just dropped from Mars.

forms: literally: let me knock on wood

examples.sr: Све иде добро, [да ку̏цнем у др̏во].
examples.en: Everything is going well, knock on wood.
I'm healthy, knock on wood.

note: You knock on wood as you say it; also «да не чује зло».

forms: literally: to go like a barefoot man through thorns

examples.sr: У тој фирми сам [про̏шао ка̏о бо̑с по тр̑њу].
examples.en: I went through a lot at that company.

examples.sr: Након развода је [про̏шла ка̏о бо̑с по тр̑њу].
examples.en: After the divorce she had a hard time.

meanings: to get caught in a vicious circle
forms: literally: to enter the fairies' round dance

examples.en: The debtor got caught in a vicious circle.

note: «врзино коло» is a magic circle you can't escape from.

examples.sr: Шта је, [ма̏чка ти је по̀јела јѐзик]?
examples.en: What's the matter, cat got your tongue?

meanings: to treasure like the apple of one's eye

examples.sr: Чува ту књигу [ка̏о о̏чи у гла́ви].
examples.en: He treasures that book like the apple of his eye.

meanings: to leave someone in the lurch

examples.en: They didn't leave me in the lurch.
Don't leave me in the lurch.

key: phr:проћи поред некога као поред турског гробља
meanings: to walk right past someone without noticing them
forms: literally: to pass someone like a Turkish cemetery

examples.sr: Прошао је поред мене [ка̏о по̏ред ту̏рског гро̏бља].
examples.en: He walked right past me as if I weren't there.

meanings: to have a huge crush on someone
forms: literally: to get fired up over someone

examples.en: He has a huge crush on her.

note: Colloquial; «ложити се» generally means to get fired up or hooked on something.

meanings: (slang) to lose one's head over someone
forms: literally: to come unglued over someone

examples.en: I'm completely crazy about her.

note: Slang; the verb «одлепити» literally means to unstick.

forms: literally: to lose one's head

examples.en: I lost my head over her.

meanings: to be taken in by someone's charm
forms: literally: to fall on someone

examples.en: I totally fell for her smile.

note: Colloquial «скроз» means completely, through and through.

forms: literally: to be mad about someone

examples.en: Marko is crazy about Maša.

note: Also used for a passion: «луд сам за сладоледом» (I'm crazy about ice cream).

meanings: to fall head over heels in love
forms: literally: to fall in love up to the ears

examples.sr: [Заљу́била] се до ушију у новог колегу.
examples.en: She fell head over heels in love with the new colleague.

forms: literally: as far as it touches me

examples.en: As far as I'm concerned, we can go.
That doesn't concern you!

note: The verb «тицати се» always takes the genitive, mostly in the 3rd person: «тиче се свих нас».

meanings: to bring up a topic in passing
forms: literally: to touch a topic

examples.sr: У разговору смо се [дота̀кли] теме путовања.
examples.en: In the conversation we touched on the topic of travel.

note: A topic is touched on briefly, without detail.

forms: literally: to turn off the topic

examples.sr: Мало смо [скре̏нули] с теме, вратимо се на оно што смо причали.
examples.en: We went a bit off topic, let's get back to what we were talking about.

note: Often said to bring the conversation back to the main point.

forms: literally: to shake out every topic

examples.sr: Седели смо сатима и [претрѐсли] сваку тему.
examples.en: We sat for hours and went over every topic.

meanings: to go through a topic inside out
to cover a topic from every angle
forms: literally: to comb a topic lengthwise and across

examples.sr: Ту тему смо [про̏чешљали] уздуж и попреко.
examples.en: We went through that topic inside out.

forms: literally: from A to Š

examples.sr: После толико година пријатељства рекли смо једно другом све [од А до Ш].
examples.en: After so many years of friendship, we told each other everything from A to Z.

note: The Serbian Cyrillic alphabet ends in Ш, so it is «од А до Ш» where English says «from A to Z».

meanings: to kill two birds with one stone
forms: literally: to kill two flies with one blow

examples.sr: Ако стигнем у пошту на путу до посла, [у̏бићу] две муве једним ударцем.
examples.en: If I stop by the post office on my way to work, I'll kill two birds with one stone.

meanings: to have a finger in every pie
forms: literally: dill in every soup

examples.sr: Он је увек [у сва̏кој чо́рбӣ] мирођија.
examples.en: He always has a finger in every pie.

note: Said about a person who interferes in everything.

forms: literally: simple as a bean

examples.en: The task is easy as pie.

forms: literally: like a calf at a painted gate

examples.sr: Стоји и гледа [ка̏о] теле у шарена врата.
examples.en: He stands there staring blankly.

forms: literally: don't paint me

examples.sr: Немој да ме [фа̏рбаш], знам да лажеш.
examples.en: Don't try to fool me, I know you're lying.

note: Colloquial «фарбати некога» means to deceive or fool someone.

meanings: to tell someone's fortune from coffee grounds
forms: literally: to look into someone's cup

examples.sr: Можеш ли да ми [по̀гледа̄ш] у шољу?
examples.en: Can you read my coffee grounds?

note: After Turkish coffee the grounds are flipped onto the saucer and the future is «read» in the patterns.

meanings: see you at the Horse (the monument on Republic Square in Belgrade)
forms: literally: see you at the horse

examples.en: See you at the Horse at six.

note: The monument to Prince Mihailo Obrenović on a horse is the traditional meeting place for Belgraders.

key: phr:леди ми се крв у жилама
forms: literally: my blood freezes in my veins

examples.sr: Кад чујем тај крик, [ле̏ди] ми се крв у жилама.
examples.en: When I hear that scream, my blood runs cold.

key: phr:срце ми је сишло у пете
meanings: my heart sank into my boots
forms: literally: my heart went down into my heels

examples.sr: Кад сам видео пса, [ср̏це] ми је сишло у пете.
examples.en: When I saw the dog, my heart sank into my boots.

meanings: to be afraid of one's own shadow
forms: literally: to be afraid of one's own shadow

examples.sr: После оног догађаја [пла̏ши] се сопствене сенке.
examples.en: Since that incident he's afraid of his own shadow.
I got goosebumps all over from fear.

note: A woman says «сва сам се најежила».

examples.en: Actually, I didn't know.

note: Written as two words: «у ствари». «Уствари» is a mistake.

examples.en: Come on, don't tell me!

note: Expresses surprise or disbelief.

forms: literally: to carry one's head in a bag

examples.en: A journalist risks his neck.

forms: literally: like magpie's legs

examples.en: He writes like chicken scratch.

meanings: to want to sink through the floor with shame
forms: literally: to cover oneself with one's ears

examples.en: I wanted to sink through the floor with shame.

note: Said about intense shame.

forms: literally: run away, bre

examples.en: Come off it, don't talk nonsense!

note: «бре» is an emotional particle expressing indignation or emphasis.

meanings: a beer to calm the nerves (rhyming joke)
forms: literally: a little beer for the nerves

examples.en: Come on, let's have a little beer for the nerves!

note: A rhyming jokey phrase, like «пиће за младиће».

examples.en: This is a cool idea!

note: The word «фора» is very versatile: a gimmick, a trick, a scheme.

meanings: to be a ball of energy, to get everything done
forms: literally: to be a dragon

examples.en: You're awesome!
He works like a beast.

note: Praise.

forms: literally: Đura sewed it for me

examples.sr: Шеф је рекао да ће нам платити хиљаду и по евра. - [Ши̏о] ми га Ђура!
examples.en: The boss said he'd pay us fifteen hundred euros. - Yeah, right!

note: After a Belgrade tailor named Đura. It used to mean quality, now it expresses disbelief.

meanings: to pay someone back in kind
forms: literally: the pleasant for the dear

examples.en: We'll pay them back in kind.

note: Can be used for good or for bad.

meanings: you're not made of glass, move out of the way
forms: literally: your dad is not a glazier

examples.en: Move over, your dad's not a glazier!

note: What fathers say to kids who block the TV.

forms: literally: to bring out rabid worms

examples.en: Don't listen to him, he's talking nonsense.

forms: literally: chicha-miche, the story is ready

examples.en: We signed and - that's that.

note: A jokey way to end a story.

meanings: April first - I trust no one

examples.en: April first - I trust no one!

note: A chant said in Serbia on April Fools' Day.

examples.en: I'm only taking carry-on luggage.
Show your boarding pass.
Please fasten your seat belts.

note: A phrase heard on a plane.

meanings: to gawk at someone as at a spectacle
forms: literally: to look as if a she-bear is dancing

examples.en: Everyone is gawking at him with their mouths open.

forms: literally: my battery is empty

examples.en: My battery is dead.
Can I charge my phone?

meanings: do you have a wine opener?

examples.en: Do you have a corkscrew?

examples.sr: Не [да̑ј] се, сад је пола посла готово!
examples.en: Don't give up, half the work is already done!

meanings: I have a knack for it
I know my way around it
forms: literally: I have a marble for that

examples.en: I have a knack for that.

note: Colloquial; «кликер» is a glass marble for playing.

examples.en: Drinks for the lads, here you go!

note: A rhyming catchphrase of waiters.

examples.en: Do you have change for twenty euros?
I care about those books.

note: The construction is «стало ми је до» + genitive.
